utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we hear the witness, I would like to know whether the parties had a chance to meet yesterday and to discuss on which document they are going to use. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take it -- referring to the -- the disputed translation of the order of the 30th of August. What's agreed between the parties at this stage is that each side can refer to its own document. We think the Prosecutor has two translations, and what we think they're going to do, and I can indicate this to you, is withdraw the one that says "command," rely on the one that uses the word "direct," and contains the additional sentence that was noticed by the witness. That matches our translation entirely with the exception of one word. Our translation, which is a CLSS translation, uses the word "control," and the OTP's version uses the word "direct." Now, that's a dispute that Mr. Gusic can't resolve because he doesn't speak English. It will be resolved later, and it need not trouble Mr. Gusic so that we can otherwise proceed with translations that match each other and it won't distract the Court or interfere with the cross-examination of this witness. Your Honour, we were inclined to -- well, sorry, we understood what Your Honour said yesterday, that as to the history of these translations, that's not a matter that should interrupt this witness because we're rushing to finish him. And I'm going to indicate how that's to be achieved in a minute, if I can.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down a little, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry. I've been asked to slow down. I will. I'm concerned about time. Your Honour, that matter of what happened with the translation can be resolved on another occasion, and it may be that when the witness Katica Miletic, who is a video witness is dealt with, we expect that she will take a small amount less than a day, so that there may be half an hour or so residual time with her, and it's not a matter for me to decide, but we would be prepared to raise the matter at that time, because it being a videolink witness and only a half-hour gap remaining, that may be an appropriate time. Could I indicate, Your Honour, that in an effort to finish this witness today, what I have done is very, very serious slashing, and it's chiefly document slashing. What it means is that I'm not going to put a number of documents to this witness because those documents can be put through other witnesses, particularly Mr. Eminovic and Mr. Dzankovic. That's what's going to happen. It may cause trouble because the witness himself may say that he wants to see the document, and in that event I'll try to control the situation as best I can, but I'm indicating that's one way I'm going to keep it short. I think we're going to save an hour by doing that because that was a significant chunk of cross-examination. I'm going to put the principles to him and move on. Your Honour, there remains a large number of documents to be dealt with today, but, however, what we would like to do is do everything we can to finish today and I think we will finish today and just reserve our right if needs be, if in fairness to the witness he needs to be confronted with the document, then we pursue the alternative that was discussed before of having a videolink with him at a later time to clean up anything that remains. And otherwise we're ready to proceed and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for your efforts. Ms. Chana, do you want to say something on this subject?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to confirm that what my learned counsel has just said is the correct position, that we are going to withdraw the first translation and rely on our second one, which says "direct." And as Mr. Morrissey indicated, now the dispute lies on the word "direct" and "control," and for the time being we are tendering our document and Mr. Morrissey is tendering his, and then later on we can resolve it by perhaps another -- another translation from CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. I believe that we have to find some other time to discuss this issue in detail. So at this stage, as the parties agrees that we will give each party's document a number so that it could be used in the courtroom. And then later on we will send those documents to the CLSS for the more authentic explanation of translation of that document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, so pursuant to that we would ask that the bundle of documents that we handed up yesterday be marked as MFI145. That's a bundle including some correspondence between CLSS and the Defence team, as it then was constituted before me, and that -- the order itself as translated, which as an exhibit should not be polluted by the other correspondence, should be marked -- the number of it is D -- Defence document 1502, and its number is DD00.2497. And it should be given the MFI number of 146.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Your Honour, based on the schedule just described by Defence counsel that they will be spending most of tomorrow -- or all day today on Mr. Gusic, most of tomorrow on Ms. Miletic, and then most of the following day on the second witness - I'm not mentioning the name because she has now indicated -- the person has indicated that they might want measures, protective measures - I would like to release the other two witnesses that are here that came in to testify that we thought we would start one today, finish it -- finish the first one sometime during Wednesday or Thursday, use both days to finish that one, and then finish the next one on Thursday. So I might as well just release both of them. There's no need for them to stay here and then stay right through the weekend. I could see if they could then come the following week the first few days maybe, if they could arrive again on Sunday and start Monday or Tuesday. But I'll -- I will re-work the schedule for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe that is the only options, you know, facing us. They may be released for this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I can assure you that I will let you go home today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's good news, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown document MFI146, that being the order of the 30th of August by Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as to paragraph number 1 there, what I put to you is this: If that document intended -- if it was the tension of the author of this that document to appoint Sefer Halilovic as a commander, then that is what would have been stated in that document; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it should state that. Although, in paragraph 2, it is somehow defined not precisely to be sure, but the team leader is appointed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And the use of the term "team leader" is quite a specific term, isn't it, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Turning to paragraph 3 now. I just want you to look at that, if you would.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 clearly gives the Chief of Staff a power to issue certain orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's also correct, isn't it, that that power to issue orders is specified to particular situations; namely, where -- sorry, in keeping with his authority and in relation to solving problems in the field. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, it is not a general commanding power at all, is it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you there though. I think it is, because in the field, to solve problems in the field, that is endowing him with part of command authority. It gives him the possibility to command. Not a great possibility, to be sure, but still a possibility to command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you this: Have a look at the preamble. And I suggest to you that the preamble provides you with the context in which he can issue those limited problem-solving orders, and that context is to eliminate current shortcomings and weaknesses in the zones of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps. Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if a unit can -- if a unit does not launch an attack although it has been ordered to do so, that means weakness, and he can deal with it on the spot. That's weakness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And, for example, if the Supreme Commander had issued a commander to a unit to go into battle on a particular day, a binding command, and the chief of the inspection team saw that that order was not complied with, the chief of the inspection team could solve that problem by ordering in accordance with the original order the recalcitrant unit to go into battle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with this order, yes. But pursuant to this paragraph, he could issue such an order even without the superior order, if the unit is prepared to carry out the task he decides should be done. There was a general order defining the conduct of combat operations, and all units were duty-bound to carry out active combat operations to liberate as much territory as possible. In this context, if through his personal information gained on the field, if he saw that a unit did not wish to go into battle or carry out a task, that it was waivering, then he could issue an order to have the unit go into battle. I am talking about offensive operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This paragraph, I wish to be very correct, gives him not a great possibility but still a possibility to command, a very limited possibility to command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And as you've indicated, it's a possibility to command that only arises where there is a problem to solve; is that correct? And I'm referring --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes. Yes. That is a limited possibility to command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Thank you. Now, the -- Mr. Gusic, I apologise for the problems that arose out of the translation yesterday, but I'd ask you now to confirm that paragraph 1 of this document requires that an inspection team be formed with the role of coordinating work. Is that correct? And I'm looking at the first line in paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the beginning of the first paragraph. Yes, "coordination." That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And really, an inspection team is no more than the eyes and ears of the main staff out on the terrain; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a large extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when paragraph 2 appoints -- well, I withdraw that. I've asked you that question already. Just excuse me a moment now, please. Okay. Thank you. Those are the questions to be asked about that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown document --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I am not satisfied with your question about paragraph 3. You dealt with half of it and not the other half, the radical half. "He must consult the commander in the case of more drastic proposals and solutions." So this has to do with the decision scheme. That would be a drastic decision. That's how I interpret it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just a moment. What I put to you is in fact what is referred to there is drastic proposals and solutions. It doesn't say "drastic orders or drastic decisions." It says "drastic proposals and solutions." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the solution, sir. This is only one part. I don't want to go into the content of this document. I believe that it is incomplete. It doesn't contain all the elements of combat disposition. In the terminology we used, this was the framework of the decision which graphically represented the fourth point of the combat order. And when I look at it, as I'd never seen the title of the Operation Neretva before or any plan of combat operations, for me it will always remain a drastic change in everything that was happening in the area of responsibility of the corps, because an active front was being opened up on a large section of the front and the units were not left the discretion of opening up pieces of the front but a very large part of the front was being opened up, and that's a drastic decision. Although, again I say this is not an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be shown document D88. Would you excuse me for a moment. I'll give you the number. It is DD00.0354, and it's to be marked as -- as MFI147.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, what you're about to be shown now is a -- another order and it's an example of another order appointing an inspection team later on in your zone of responsibility in October of 1993. Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you confirm that an inspection team led by Asim Dzambasovic, actually present in court today, was sent to the 6th Corps area? Do you agree with that? At a time shortly after 21st of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen this order, and I don't remember the team being in the area of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you don't recall it, that's okay. I just want to ask you something about the form of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the following page please be shown. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that following page?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this inspection team has a variety of functions such as reviewing organisation, checking the work of the commands, and cooperating and establishing contact with the authorities? Do you see that? I understand I'm rushing through it here, Mr. Gusic, but --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown the following page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 4, and in particular look at the last section of that -- sorry, paragraph 5. I'm sorry. We've got a note on it. Paragraph 5 indicates: "The team leader will occasionally sent reports to me" - that being Rasim Delic - "The team leader with occasionally send reports to me on the situation on the ground and proposals for orders to improve work."

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that. I just have the authorisation before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you have -- do you have a paragraph 5 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't. I have the authorisation listing seven members of the team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You will have to ask that -- perhaps in the Bosnian version one page go back. The Bosnian version is differently paginated to the -- the English, the Australian version.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now: "The team leader will from time to time deliver a report."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the next sub: "In urgent cases, he will resolve a situation by giving an order on the spot." Now, do you see that para there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I take it an example of the same sort of problem-solving power that you referred to earlier in -- in the order which we just looked at before dated 30th of August.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But it's not the same. It's essentially different from what we spoke about before. There's an important difference. In the first part there, it says "solve problems on the spot." It doesn't define urgency or the category of the problem. Whereas, here it says "submit proposals." In the other document, it says, as far as I can recall it, "inform me or consult me about any drastic decisions," whereas, here it says "in urgent situations resolve the situation on the ground, on the spot." So that's a big difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand what you put there, but do you acknowledge this, that in general terms it is a usual feature of inspection teams to give the team leader of the inspection team some small and limited power to issue orders of a problem-solving kind? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is what I consider to be usual in the case of teams; whereas, the first order is a bit broader than what is generally understood as the powers of an inspection team. Whereas, here it defines what is necessary for an inspection field to operate on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. I'm now going to take you briefly to the chronology of the days between -- the days when the inspection team arrived in -- to Herzegovina. On the 1st of September -- and this is now a period of chronology that will take you from their arrival up until the Dobro Polje conference on the 5th of September. Do you understand that? Okay.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 1st of September, Sefer Halilovic arrived in Herzegovina and did he meet with you along with Sevko Hodzic, Selmo Cikotic, and other officers to discuss the potential for combat operations in your area?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I told you at the outset I cannot stand by any dates, because I didn't note down any dates. They exist in the operational records, but I accept the date. I cannot confirm that that's the date without looking at the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I understand your reservation about the date. But generally speaking, when Halilovic first arrived in Herzegovina, do you agree that you had such a meeting with him, Cikotic, other commanders, and in the presence of Sevko Hodzic, the journalist?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether Brigadier Cikotic was there or not. Sevko Hodzic was one of the permanent members of the team, and almost always when the general was in the area of responsibility of the corps Sevko Hodzic was with him. Almost always. I can't say always, but very frequently. I did meet the general in early September, but which other officers were present, I couldn't say at present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At that meeting and bearing in mind the preparations that had already been going on for combat activities in the zone of responsibility of the 6th Corps, which you have already acknowledged, do you agree that you discussed in detail with Sefer Halilovic the potential lines of attack by Bosnian army forces in order to relieve Mostar and unblock the road between Jablanica and Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this word "in detail," that's more than we were able to discuss at that meeting, but we did talk about the various possibilities; however, a detailed analysis of the lines of attack would take more than a single meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zulfikar Alispago present at that meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure. He probably was, but I'm not certain. He probably was though because he was always there when the general was in the zone of responsibility. I cannot say with full certainty that he was there, but he was almost always there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in the days following that meeting, I suggest to you that the -- the senior staff members -- I was going to call them "old soldiers." I'll ask you a question about that in a moment. The senior staff member, Suljevic, Bilajac, and Karic, along with Sefer Halilovic, commenced to work on plans to attack along the lines which you in the 6th Corps had already commenced to plan. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that much is true. They had already commenced to work on things that were the subject already of our own plans. But we hadn't yet gun to realise, to implement those plans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, I understand that you do not acknowledge seeing that map that is next to you, and by these questions I'm not seeking to suggest that you have acknowledged it. But what I want to put to you is this: That the map Neretva 93 discloses lines of attack that were exactly what the 6th Corps had been planning for a week before the inspection team even arrived in Herzegovina. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to respond to this. I had thought we had already established a normal relationship and we would not resort to insults, but I'm really insulted by this approach of yours. If you tell me you find me responsible, say so clearly. If the general stands up and tells me you were responsible, you were in command, I will say okay, I'm guilty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But please don't let me go back to Sarajevo without allowing me to tell you what I want.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't be unfair. I don't want to stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stop stopping me. You shouldn't have provoked me. After having provoked me, why do you want to stop me? You shouldn't have called me here in the first place if you won't let me say what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, please cool down. I believe that the Defence counsel just asked you a very simple question, a very simple question. And -- and I also believe that we come across this issue yesterday. I don't think, in my view, that Defence counsel is blaming you. He just wants to know a very simple fact. If you do not agree with what the Defence counsel said, you may say so. There's no problem about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not say the Defence counsel was blaming me, but he said in a nice way -- he put it to me that I was lying. I said from the very beginning I am not saying what people want to hear. I'm saying the truth, and the truth is I have never seen this map before it was shown to me right here. I stated so right at the beginning and right at the beginning I asked the kind lawyer not to ask me questions of that kind; otherwise, I am prepared to say that I have made mistakes, I have made errors, and I stand by them and I am prepared to be held responsible for the errors that I really made, but not this one, because I was not involved in that. All I have to fear is God himself and nobody shall call me a liar just like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown document 119, that's Defence document 119. It's DD00.0514, and it's to be marked for identification as 148.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being brought up on the screen, Mr. Gusic, I indicate to you that this is an order from Stjepan Siber to the 6th Corps dated the 4th of September. Do you have that order in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... some formal facts about it, and you can just agree or disagree whether this is the case. The order is dated the 4th of September and it is from Stjepan Siber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just as a matter of interest on the deputy question from yesterday, would you look and see the way in which Siber -- Mr. Siber signed himself as standing in for the commander deputy? Do you notice that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could I just ask -- let me ask the questions for a moment. You indicated yesterday that perfectly understandably, I might comment, that you couldn't recall exactly what the practice was in terms of signing as deputy at different times but you were prepared to accept that there was a practice like this at one time. Now, seeing this document, do you agree that that was the practice in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have said before that this looks authentic to me, everything that was written in the official logbooks of the army I am prepared to accept, and there were several formats. This is probably one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's all I wanted to know. Now, Mr. Gusic, that is a combat order directed from the deputy commander, Siber, to the 6th Corps command and not to the IKM or to Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that point -- well, I withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. I offer that for tender, that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I have a question arises out of the 4th of September of another kind: Did Commander Delic arrive in Herzegovina on the 4th of September? Let me ask --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm already --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question another way. I'm sorry. It does contain the date problem, so I'll ask the question another day. On a date somewhere early in September, do you agree that Commander Delic arrived in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that he attended at a meeting in Jablanica -- in fact, at Donja Jablanica, with Sefer Halilovic and other senior commanders, including Zulfikar Alispago?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend that meeting, but I know that the commander did have a meeting in Jablanica. I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the most senior 6th Corps official who was present at that meeting? Was it Mr. Fazlic or another officer?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I think it was Fazlic, but I'm not certain. I think my deputy, Bahrudin Fazlic, was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. And after that meeting, you met with Commander Delic at the 6th Corps command in Konjic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right after the meeting -- in fact, I can't really say whether it was the same day or the day after, but after that Commander Delic did drop by the command of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or rather, more precisely, the ARK building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I'll come to the ARK building in a moment but the fact is that Commander Delic came and spent many hours with you at Konjic on the night of the 4th and he stayed the night there as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a night in the month of September that he spent in the ARK building. I don't know exactly when. And I had the honour and privilege of spending quite a long time together with him in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, Mr. Gusic, I put it to you that the chief topic of conversation with him was nothing else than Neretva 93, the operation which he had just signed the map of that very afternoon before he met you. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. He did not mention the Neretva operation to me in a single word, not a single time. So even then I did not receive that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you stick with your story that you -- with your account that you gave to this Tribunal in the evidence in chief that the first you heard of Operation Neretva 93 is when you collected or when you -- when you arranged the transport of Sarajevo units in your 6th Corps trucks? Do you retain that -- do you stay with that account?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even then did I know the name of that operation. All I knew was that there were preparations that should eventually result in combat operations but that it was called the "Neretva 93 operation" is something I didn't know. I found out the name only after the whole operation was completed. I'm talking only about the name, Neretva 93; although I was aware, I admit, of the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're saying that commander Delic, who was your commander, and Bahrudin Fazlic, who was your deputy, didn't tell you the name of this operation on the 4th of September? That is your honest evidence, is it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my most honest evidence. They did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if that's the case. That night at Konjic, did Sefer Halilovic also stay in Konjic at a premises called the ARK, the A-R-K?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I believe he did, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that the Tribunal understands some Konjic geography at which may become important later, your command -- I don't need the details. I just need these facts. Your command was located in one part of Konjic; the ARK was a JNA facility with an antinuclear bunker that was positioned near to Konjic. Are both those facts correct so far as they go?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is close by now, nowadays, but at that time it was very far away, a whole lifetime away, because they were separated by a clearance; whereas, the ARK building was constantly under fire. In the conditions in which we found ourselves, it was light years away, because it was constantly being fired upon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Gusic. Could I just ask you one other question about the geography which may be important: From Konjic to Jablanica in peacetime is a relatively quick journey. How long did it take in wartime, and, in particular September 1993, approximately, to get from Konjic to Jablanica, and was the main road open at all?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main road was not open. It took half a day, depending on the vehicle you had. If it was an all-terrain vehicle, you could reach it sooner. If you had a simple passenger car, it took half a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Very well. Now, what I want to put to you now -- I'm turning now to the 5th, so we're actually making some progress. I'm going to move now to the 5th of September. After you woke up in Konjic -- or sorry, perhaps one other question about the 4th of September. Before you came back to Konjic on the 4th of September, I put to you that you attended with Delic and Sefer Halilovic at an inspection of the 45th Brigade or some elements of the 45th Brigade at Buturovic Polje prior to coming back to the ARK. Do you agree that that took place?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes. Most likely, yes. I cannot say with 100 per cent certainty, but probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I understand that. Now, dish Now -- I will now turn to what happened on the day of the Dobro Polje meeting. Now, Mr. Gusic, there was in fact a meeting of commanders at Dobro Polje on the 5th of September. And if you don't recall the date, that's okay. But do you agree that there was such a meeting at around that time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, Sefer Halilovic discussed with -- perhaps I should ask you this: At that meeting, there were numerous of the commanders of the -- of the units below corps level, in particular Hasan Hakanovic, the commander of the 317th division, Zejnilagic, Mr. Cikotic was there, and Mr. Buza, the commander of the Independent Prozor Battalion. Do you agree that those persons were present?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were more people. There were certain associates of commanders and there was a large number of people, and those you mentioned were there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And -- well, thank you for that, because I was going to put to you that other lesser commanders were there as well. Now, at that meeting, it is the fact that Sefer Halilovic -- and were also -- I should ask you this: Were there members of staff of the inspection team there, Karic, Bilajac, Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at that meeting, did Karic, Bilajac, Suljevic and Sefer Halilovic indicate to the lesser commanders - and I don't mean "lesser commanders" in an insulting way. I'm just referring to them as lower-order commanders - did the inspection team members, including Halilovic, there explain to those lesser commanders the tasks that they would be required to fulfil in the course of Operation Neretva 93?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most of the talk concentrated on Buza, the commander of the independent battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, I'm not going to go into the details of what each one was told at this point, but thank you for confirming the general question. You have indicated in the past that Sefer Halilovic resubordinated some of your 6th Corps units into the Operation Neretva 93. Do you agree that that's been your position?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And do you say that that took place here at Dobro Polje when these tasks were explained to the units?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you say that it happened at a later time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- are you in a position to point to a written order, or even a written order number, under which that supposed resubordination took place?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot because I haven't seen any orders. I saw one order when I was proofed by the Prosecutor, and even that was the first time I saw it. And I can't produce the order anyway to prove what I'm saying, except the order that was shown to me by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was this order that was shown to you by the Prosecutor, Mr. Gusic? First of all, what date was it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date. I wasn't memorising dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- at any point, but it was an order appointing the commander for the axis of attack, the late Enver Zejnilagic, and determining -- or, rather, directing the 317th, 400-something Brigade, and another brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter misses the numbers of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to become engaged with only one copy being sent to files. Not even the archives of the corps. It is possible that there is an order dating before that time, but I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So the order you were shown was an order --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the order which is MFI124. I don't want there to be any doubt about which order we're talking about here. Could the witness please be shown that, MFI124. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that order in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the order I was shown by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. You're going to be questioned about this order in about an hour's time, but at this stage it's sufficient to put -- look at the top and see if that order is dated at Voljevac on the 15th of September, 1993. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. All right. And, of course, did the -- I should ask -- well, I won't. I'll come to that in a minute. All right. Thank you for that. So that that's the only written order that you're able to point this Tribunal to whereby 6th Corps units, you say, are resubordinated by Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I wasn't looking nor was I intending to produce a written order. Maybe there are other written orders. What was the reality on the ground was that General Halilovic was the real authority there and those units there did not need a written order to enable him to engage them. This is - and that's the only thing I'm saying - that this is the only order I have ever seen, and it -- I didn't even know about it until I was shown it by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Gusic, look, at the moment I've just dealt with -- you understand I've got to deal with some de jure command responsibility allegations by this Prosecutor. I'll come to the de facto point now, given your comments. Mr. Gusic, I want to put some propositions to you here, and there's no need to be personally insulted by it. This is a Tribunal and contentions of fact arise, and this is one. I want to put it to you that when Sefer Halilovic gave the instructions that he gave at Dobro Polje and later, he gave those instructions in accordance with two things and two things only: First of all, his role as Chief of Staff under Delic pursuant to the map that's behind you and, secondly, pursuant to the occasional problem-solving power, the limited problem-solving power that he had as head of the inspection team. Now, do you agree with that proposition or do you disagree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, it's not for me to agree or disagree. He knows himself on what basis he issued orders. And I have no intention of agreeing or disagreeing. General Halilovic knows best what gave him the powers to issue orders. He may have had other things to rely on that I have never had the opportunity to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Now, I want to put a proposition to you here, and you indicated last week we were going to part company. Here we are about to part company. But I want to put that this is to you quite clearly so that you know where the questions are headed. I put to you that after Dobro Polje and up to and including and after the Uzdol incident, you personally did retain a commanding role as commander of the 6th Corps over the units on that map, the Independent Prozor Battalion, the detached parts of the 44th and 45th Brigade, the Sutjeska Brigade and the 317th or such a part of that as took part in the battles. Now, I have to ask you, although I understand your answer is going to be no: Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with that proposition. I was on the side -- I sided with the commander of the Independent Prozor Battalion in a very heartfelt way when he disagreed that this attack should be executed in the way it was ordered, and I agreed with that. I did not agree with the execution of any combat operations along that axis. The information that you have, that you are relying upon, is probably incorrect, because -- and I will leave it for the end -- or maybe I can say now what I wanted to say from the beginning yesterday. I questioned the credibility of your Defence witness Asim Dzambasovic because in the beginning of last year, early last year, he attempted to take a statement from Mr. Dautovic regarding the circumstances in a way that differed from the reality of what happened in Dobro Polje. And that failed. After that, a certain Mrs. or Miss Edina took it upon herself to harass his wife, the man whose statement they wanted to take, and she offered to give him the Prosecutor's telephone number because he is more inclined allegedly to act as a Prosecution witness than as a Defence witness, although I wouldn't understand why, and perhaps Mr. Halilovic knows this. Perhaps he doesn't. But I don't think he would support it anyway, because he doesn't need to be supported by false witnesses. On the 6th of September --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stop there --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- they met with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... before we go to the 6th of September, this allegation you're making about Dzambasovic, did you tell the police about that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that, and I wanted to finish. I've been wanting to tell you this since the beginning of the day yesterday to avoid this situation. I was held responsible by --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I would ask the witness to be directed to answer the original question and not to -- whatever justification he may feel he has, and I don't want to enter into that. This is non-response, and I ask that he be -- now be asked to come back to the path.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken to the carpet by the commander over this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Gusic, could I just come back to the issues in the case. You do not dispute that the following units were 6th Corps units prior to being -- I think I've asked you that, but I'll just make sure it's right -- the Independent Prozor Battalion, the 44th Brigade, the 45th Brigade, and 317th, and the Sutjeska Battalion were all part of the 6th Corps prior to what you say was a resubordination to the IKM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that there's no written order. I won't ask you about that again. But what I -- now, you've indicated that you can't recall the precise dates, and I understand that, but is it the fact that to your knowledge the 317th Brigade and attached battalions to it launched an attack one day on an area including a hill called Black Top - Crni Vrh, I think is the pronunciation - and that only on the following day did Enver Buza and his Independent Prozor Battalion launch their part of the -- the attack. Now, do you agree with that, that the 317th and its units attacked on one day and the following day Buza went in to attack with his Independent Prozor Battalion? Is that the fact?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of these details. I wasn't up there and I wasn't commanding those troops. Whatever I say might be wrong. I will say, however, that even before the time you're referring to, combat operations were executed along the axes you mentioned. And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so just stay with this. What I'm asking about is: The order of things was the 317th attacked and next -- and Buza failed to go into attack, so that the next morning Buza and the Independent Prozor Battalion went into the attack. Do you agree that that's what you were told happened?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I commanded those troops, I would be able to tell you, but I cannot say. I cannot confirm this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you can't confirm it. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Defence document D476. I'll just provide the proper number in a moment. It is DD00.2185. And it's to be marked for Exhibit 149.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have that document in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that document a report from the Independent Prozor Battalion to the 6th Corps command?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This does have the form of a report. I would have to read the document to refresh my memory of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm going to give you every opportunity to read this document. You can be sure, Mr. Gusic. But let's just start with the headline part of it. Is that -- is the fact that it's addressed to the 6th Corps command? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And is it from the Prozor Independent Battalion and does it have the form of a report?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, just read through it. And on the first line, does it say that "Pursuant to attack order operative number" -- and I want you to notice this number, please -- "01/1500-27 of 11th of September, the Prozor Independent Battalion units infiltrated deep into enemy territory as planned in the night between 13 and 14 September 1993 with the aim of" -- and it goes on to spell out what the aims were? Now, do you notice that? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can see here that what the Prozor Independent Battalion say they were doing is following an order and they give the order number. It's order number 01/1500-27 of 11 September 1993. Now, you understand that orders are given operative numbers so as to be able to be identified; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what appears to be happening here; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I would like to see this order of the 11th of September, who issued it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, just let's -- let's persist with this order first and we'll see what happens after that. Could the -- have you finished reading that page or do you need a bit more time to read it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you read, I'll ask you a general question, and you may find yourself able to respond. It appears to be the Prozor Independent Battalion reporting upon its actions during the attack on Uzdol on the night of the 13th and the morning of the 14th of September, 1993. Do you agree with that broad proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see from this that they are reporting to the corps command. If this is an authentic document, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turn over the page, please. Sorry, perhaps I shouldn't demand that you turn it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness have the page turned over so that he can see what follows, and perhaps the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have the second page before you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And do you see here -- and this is something that may come up with another witness, but I'd better stress it with you. Buza gives an estimate that "65 Croatian soldiers and 30 civilians, mostly armed, were liquidated during the entire operation. One should bear in mind that the Ustasha artillery was literally destroying the entire Uzdol sector the whole time." Now, was Buza there giving an account of the dead on the Croat side to you, the -- or sorry, perhaps -- to the 6th Corps command? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And at the bottom, does the conclusion say: "This report and the overall data have been made available to General Staff Chief Sefer Halilovic, Colonel Vehbija Karic, and Colonel Zicro Suljevic, who monitored" - and you note that word "monitored" - "the whole operation from the observation post?" Do you see that conclusion that's noted there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And then do you see that in the end it's indicated that it's addressed to the 6th Corps command and to the files; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, you don't dispute that you received this report from Enver Buza, do you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never seen it like this. This is the first time I see this report, because the conclusion down there, I would certainly have recalled it had I seen it before. As for the information you've mentioned, 65, 30, there was a similar report mentioning the number of casualties in these operations. I can't say it's exactly the same, but I did see a similar report which I received from Buza. Having learned of this, I asked about the losses. But as for the time when I saw it, that is something I cannot confirm at this moment. But this is the first time I've seen the report in this form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the information in the report was all communicated to you, including the order number; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command and not to me. They came to the corps command. But yes, I should have seen this. I was supposed to have seen this. This is an important report, and I was supposed to have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer it for tender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To this matter -- could I please have the witness now shown Exhibit -- Defence document D271, and the number of that is DD00.0416 -- sorry, I take that back. It's DD00.1416 - I have no idea how I came up with that - and the MFI number would be 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a document which is going to come up on the screen. Is it? Okay. Do you have this --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... very well

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document -- I was shown it by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Okay. Now, in -- in looking at that document, does this appear to be an order to attack and when it's turned over it will become clear, and I'll take you to that page in a moment -- but when it's turned over, it will become clear that it was an order by Mr. Zejnilagic who was the commander of the 317th. Now, is that what it appears to be, an attack order by Mr. Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not that it appears to be. The first part is a typical combat order in form. Yes, that's what it is, what I've seen so far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you just look carefully, please, at the preamble, where it says: "On the basis of the order of the NGS Chief of General Staff" -- and I'll just stop there. That's -- although it doesn't name Sefer Halilovic, the fact is Sefer Halilovic was that person; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it goes on. It says: "On the basis of the order of the NGS Chief of Staff and the command of the commander of the 6th Corps OP." And then it gives an operative number which is -- which I put to you is an order number: "01/1500-27 of 11 September 1993." So does Zejnilagic base his order for the attack explicitly in this document on an order from the Chief of Staff, that's obviously Sefer Halilovic, and on a written order number -- a written number with an order number attached to it from the 6th Corps -- from the commander 6th Corps? Do you agree that that's the dual basis on which Zejnilagic appears to be acting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here. That's correct. As I had an opportunity of seeing this document and the order OP 01/150-27, when talking to the Prosecutor, but I'd never seen it before, I can say that I did not issue or approve this order. It was not issued by me. This morning --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I have my passport with me, and you can see my signature in it. It has not changed in 26 years. So you can see for yourself whether this is a document I signed and approved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll come to that issue about who signed it in just a moment, Mr. Gusic, but as you can see, the clues are beginning to point very clearly, aren't they, to the fact that there's an order from the 6th Corps command with a particular number on it? Do you agree with that? Because now it's turned up in Buza's report and in this order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And looking at the detail of this order now, if you wouldn't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we just go down to point 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where you can see the -- the axis of attack. While you're look at point number 4, Mr. Gusic, if you need to turn over the page, you'd better indicate, because you've got a Bosnian version, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the court staff assist by turning to the following page in the English version. And perhaps Mr. Gusic can indicate if he needs that done too.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I can see paragraph 4, and it's written: "According to the standards and procedures that are in use." It specifies the manoeuvre, the axes of attack, the combat readiness, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it's all entirely consistent with what's on that map right behind you which you have never seen before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is far more precise than can be seen on the map. The terrain specified is much narrower and more precise, and that's as it should be. Because we already have the focus expressed, the directions of attack, the manoeuvre is defined. Assignments are given. The combat disposition is specified. Combat readiness is specified. The command post is specified. Even the next command post, because the commander assesses that the operation will be successful. So it contains everything it should.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And would you look, please, at the date that is specified for the attack that's contained in that paragraph; namely, the date of the 16th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can see -- going back -- oh, sorry, perhaps I won't go back just yet. Yes, could you please now just go back -- could we go back to the first page once again. Very well. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just scroll up a bit, please. I can see the beginning of the document, the first part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to direct you to --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I can see it all. Now I can see the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you can see that this is a document which was issued -- an order to attack which was issued on the 15th of September contemplating attacks to take place on the 16th of September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that for tender, that document. Could the witness now please be shown Defence Exhibit D270. That is DD00.1414, and it's MFI151.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, this is a short letter, and I want you to read it but first just to identify the dates. Firstly, do you agree that it is a letter addressed to the command of the 6th Corps to the commander personally and that it's come from a man called Commander Enes Kovacevic? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's dated as being sent from Jablanica on the 13th of September, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kovacevic was the commander of the 44th Mountain Brigade, the headquarters of which was based in Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in reading this letter out -- and I'm going to take you through it. This letter provides: "On the 11th of September at 2000 hours, I briefed the chief of the Supreme Command Staff about the possibilities of combat operations on the Jablanica-Gracanica axis, and after this a request was sent to the command of the 6th Corps for supply of the necessary materiel and technical equipment. During the evening of 11 September, the corps commander informed me in person in a telephone conversation about the activities of the 45th Mountain Brigade and promised the equipment where needed." Now, do you agree that there's no room for doubt here that Kovacevic is talking about a conversation with you personally?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following paragraph: "During 12 September, we were expecting the corps commander to come in -- to come in order to work out the details for the next combat operations, but we have not so far received anything concrete regarding the planned combat operations nor the material support we are asking you to inform us about the following." And he goes on: "In the 44th -- is the 44th Brigade going to receive the requested equipment to conduct combat operations and is the 45th Brigade going to conduct combat operations, and on which axis? And how are we going to work out coordinated action?" Now, do you see what I've just read out in -- before your eyes in this court -- in this Tribunal, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that letter, I put to you, indicates plainly that you had discussed with Kovacevic not just some supply of materials and not just some other topic that enabled you not to mention the word "Neretva 93" but direct and obvious combat operations explicitly spelled out more than once; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, if you were a soldier, I would challenge what you said. But I appreciate that you are probably an excellent lawyer. I understand the way you're putting your question and the context in which you're putting it. However, this doesn't say that I am leading the operations or commanding them. What the commander of the 44th Brigade is asking me, these are questions of joint operations and the success of the 44th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 45th Brigade. Interpreter's apology.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 45th was my brigade, and I had to take care of the men and what was going on. Let me remind you that unfortunately in that period I lost a very good man and good commander from that brigade. It was my obligation - and I still feel this today - to be aware of what my men were doing and what was happening to them; however, this does not indicate that I was assigning the tasks. As I would apply to my father for help, the brigade commander was asking me for help to give him the information he needed for his combat operations. He probably didn't get the information he needed, which is why he applied to the corps command for help in carrying out the combat operations. This, however, does not indicate that the corps commander was actually leading the operations. We were just providing support on the ground, and we certainly did this. However, it did not lead the combat operations. It did not directly command the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic -- well, I'll go on to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I tender that document. Sorry, I offer that document for tender at this point. Your Honour, I now want to show the document -- show the witness a document. It's D1500 -- would you just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document received by us from the Prosecution. It hasn't been uploaded into the system, so we must now commit an act of treachery against the e-court system, which we'll rectify as soon as we can but rather than delay the witness, we'd just as soon proceed by paper copies if we can for now. Thank you. And could Mr. Gusic be provided with the -- a Bosnian original, please. Your Honours, we'd ask that this be marked for exhibit, MFI152.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Mr. Gusic, this is a document provided by the Prosecutor. I'll give you the chance to read it in a moment. But I just want you to confirm some formal matters about it first of all. Firstly, is this a document that's headed "Order to attack," operation number 01/1500-27?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the number that was referred to in the Buza report which we looked at earlier and also the Zejnilagic attack order which we looked at earlier?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this order to attack now on the face of it a document emanating from the 6th Corps and in particular the command of the 6th Corps? I'll come to the person who signed it in a minute, but is that what it says that, it comes from the 6th Corps from Dobro Polje on the 11th of September?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here that this is a document drawn up in Dobro Polje on the 11th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I want to take you through some details of this document. And I ask you, first of all: In form, the form of this document, is the form of a combat order given by a commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is more or less at the level of the battalion commander, but this is a very meagre order. It contains some elements, but it is not written in the best way. However, this is at the level of battalion commander. If I were marking it, I would fail it actually as an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I won't go into school issues at this stage, Mr. Gusic. I'll just stick to the text. Does this document explicitly detach a company from the Independent Prozor Battalion, a company from the 45th Brigade, a battalion from the 317th Brigade, and two platoons from the Sutjeska Battalion, which was a unit from Foca? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, when I asked you questions before about the Buza -- well, and I'll come back to that in a minute. The axis of the attack described in this document is completely consistent once again with what's marked on the big map which you say you've never seen of Neretva 93 right behind you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the map, I don't see the Prozor Independent Battalion, but it's probably within the 317th Brigade, and the axis is here, so I have no reason to doubt what you say. You have probably checked it. I don't see the Prozor Independent Battalion, but it's probably there as part of the 317th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the -- at the order to attack that you have in front of you here, you'll note in paragraph 1 in the second-last -- or it's possibly the third-last sentence -- the third-last short sentence makes reference to units which are facing the Uzdol sector and also to a minefield that's placed there. Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what paragraph? Sorry? In 1?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first paragraph. It's the very end of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes. Now I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, Mr. Gusic, you're indicating that you have seen this document before but you're saying that you only just saw it when you were with the Prosecutors. Can you indicate how long ago it was that you saw this -- this document, according to you, for the first time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it last Tuesday or Wednesday, about a week ago, seven or eight days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just in case my memory is playing me tricks, you don't recall mentioning this order or any of the other ones that I have referred you to when you gave your evidence in chief to this Tribunal. You didn't mention them at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't shown to me. But in the process of proofing, this order has been shown to me here in this building. That was the first time I saw it in this format.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Gusic, the fact of the matter is that either you or someone signing on your behalf issued this combat order on the 11th of the 9th. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had not signed the order. I can show you my signature; that hasn't changed in 26 years. If you find a single document signed in a different way, that would be amazing. Have a look at my signature. If you find any other kind of signature allegedly pertaining to me, I'll take back every word. But I -- this particular signature, I've never seen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've got no objection to the witness displaying his signature, if that's what he wishes to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But you may ask some questions about the signature in the document, whether, you know, the witness knew who really signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could I just ask you this before we come to -- just holding that document there, if you don't mind. I'm sorry to do that. You wouldn't really dignify the signature on the -- the scrawl on the document as being a signature at all, would you, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one on the document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one on the document. That's what I'm talking about. Can you say that that refers to any letter of the alphabet that you know?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look at my own signature. It may not look like any particular letter of the alphabet, but I can read my name and surname in it. I think a signature is a personal thing and it identifies us. If we are now talking about this document, what should have been done was to write the full name of the person who drew up and signed this order. It is not proper to only initial such documents, because this looks like an initial rather than a signature. It is not proper procedure. Both the addressee and the author should be clearly identified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Well, I'll -- although, Mr. Gusic, feel free to refer to the signatures at any time you need to, but I don't need the court usher -- the court staff to continue doing what they are now doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But could we leave the -- leave that -- the original document on the ELMO like that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, this document you indicated was a relatively poorly drafted document, and what I want to put to you is that it really does look as if it was drafted hastily, doesn't it, Mr. Gusic? Quickly.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it was drafted, under what circumstances, but there is quite a lot missing in it, not specified. It's probably something done in haste and something that was not properly done by a full team of people normally expected to participate in drafting a document of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the -- and the pen marks or the writing marks near to the word "komandant"," you don't dispute this: They might have been done in haste as well, mightn't they?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, "komandant" -- which komandant? It could be battalion commander, brigade commander, army commander. What commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Gusic, could I ask you --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title is a title.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But the question I'm going to ask you is: Were you at Dobro Polje on the 11th of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th September, I can't tell you where I was, but I certainly wasn't at Dobro Polje, because if I had been there, I would certainly have seen this document. I know for sure that I was not in Dobro Polje on the 11th of September. If this was written on the 11th of September in Dobro Polje, then I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was your deputy, Fazlic, present in Dobro Polje on that occasion, or your Chief of Staff, Tirak, present in Dobro Polje on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tirak could not have been in Dobro Polje, and Bahrudin Fazlic could possibly have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. And, Mr. Gusic, just in relation to this document, you agree that that document has been referred to by other commanders within the 6th Corps zone of responsibility, Buza and Zejnilagic, in the week following -- or I won't say "the week," but in the nine days following this document. And what I want to ask you is this: Did you ever tell them or ask them what on earth they were referring to in ascribing a command document to the commander of the 6th Corps with a particular number identifying it when you personally had never signed any such document nor knew anything about it?
